title: Prevalence of gingival overgrowth induced by calcium channel blockers: a community-based study
authors: Ellis JS, Seymour RA, Steele JG, Robertson P, Butler TJ, Thomason JM
population: Patients recruited from general medical practices in north-east England: 442 taking nifedipine, 181 amlodipine, 186 diltiazem and 102 controls
funder: not read: the publisher page returns HTTP 403, and PubMed and Europe PMC list no grants.
result: Significant gingival overgrowth was seen in 6.3% of subjects taking nifedipine, more than with amlodipine, diltiazem or controls; the prevalence with amlodipine or diltiazem did not differ significantly from controls. Within the nifedipine group severity was related to gingival inflammation, and men were 3 times as likely as women to develop overgrowth. The authors cite earlier prevalence estimates from 20% to 83% for calcium channel blockers in general and a single earlier estimate of 3.3% for amlodipine.
